name: Maintenance Checklist
description: A general maintenance checklist for keeping facilities and equipment in safe working order.

items.text: List the buildings, systems and equipment that need maintenance.
Set the inspection frequency for each asset.
items.note: Follow manufacturer intervals and your organization's procedures.

items.text: Gather manuals, service histories and asset records.
Confirm spare parts, consumables and tools are in stock.
Assign tasks to qualified staff or contractors.
Review safety requirements and permits before starting.
Wear the required personal protective equipment.
Isolate energy sources and apply lockout/tagout before work.
Verify equipment is fully de-energized before servicing.
Check emergency stops, guards and interlocks operate correctly.
Test fire alarms, extinguishers and emergency lighting.
Confirm first aid kits and spill kits are stocked and accessible.
Inspect machines for wear, damage, leaks and corrosion.
Check belts, chains, bearings and moving parts for wear.
Lubricate components per the manufacturer's schedule.
Clean filters, vents and cooling systems.
Check fluid levels and top up or replace as needed.
Test equipment under normal operating conditions.
Calibrate instruments and gauges where required.
Inspect roofs, walls, doors and windows for damage.
Check floors, stairs and walkways for trip and slip hazards.
Test lighting and replace failed lamps.
Inspect plumbing for leaks and check water systems.
Check HVAC operation and replace air filters.
Keep entrances, exits and grounds clear and well maintained.
Inspect electrical panels, cables and outlets for damage.
Check for overheating, loose connections or burning smells.
Test backup generators and uninterruptible power supplies.
Verify metering and monitoring systems are working.
Inspect compressed air, gas and water utilities for leaks.
Confirm only qualified electricians work on live systems.
Record each task, the date and who completed it.
Log any faults, readings and parts replaced.
Raise work orders for repairs that cannot be done immediately.
Track recurring issues to plan replacements or upgrades.
Update service histories and asset records.
Review the maintenance schedule and adjust intervals as needed.

faq.a: It is a structured list of routine tasks for keeping a facility and its equipment safe and reliable, covering inspections, cleaning, lubrication, safety checks and repairs so nothing is overlooked between service intervals.

faq.q: How often should maintenance tasks be done?
faq.a: It depends on the asset and how hard it works. Group tasks into daily, weekly, monthly and annual routines, and follow the intervals in the manufacturer's manual and your organization's procedures.
Facility managers, maintenance technicians and equipment operators. It works as a shared routine so anyone on shift can complete and sign off the same standard checks.

faq.q: What is the difference between this and a preventive maintenance checklist?
faq.a: This is a general upkeep routine for day-to-day reliability. A preventive maintenance checklist is a scheduled program of planned tasks tied to specific assets, intervals and records, often managed in a CMMS.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the maintenance checklist for the maintenance room or clipboard, or download the PDF to log completed tasks, note issues and keep signed records on file.
